title: Sebastian and the Ember
premise: Wendell Ishikawa, a mercenary whose god Ember went silent a decade ago, is dragged back into the world when a dying courier presses him a map to the court beneath Thornfell—where the usurper Vaelric holds stolen souls as currency. The map's final destination is Wendell himself: the soul it marks belongs to his lost sister, sold by their father to buy the family's survival. Guided by Sera, a smuggler-priestess who still hears Ember's whispers, Wendell must cross the mountains ahead of Vaelric's armies, choosing between loyalty to the mercenary company that raised him and the truth of what his father did. In the court beneath the mountain, Wendell learns Ember never went silent—it was imprisoned, its voice harvested—and he trades his own name and memories to free both god and sister. He returns hollow but whole enough, leading the free cities' defense with Sera carrying what he can no longer remember.
about_author: Lior Reyes is a former mountain guide who turned to fantasy after a winter stranded in a fire lookout with nothing but notebooks and folklore. Their work explores debts we inherit and the gods we outgrow.

chapters.title: The Silent Altar
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. On a rain-soaked contract in Thornfell's foothills, Wendell finishes a job for his mercenary company and privately visits a dead altar where he once heard the god Ember speak. Nothing answers, as always for ten years. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Last Mile
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A bleeding stranger stumbles into Wendell's camp on the smugglers' road, pursued by riders in Vaelric's colors. With his last breath the man presses a wax-sealed map into Wendell's hands and says a name that stops his heart: Ishikawa. Emotional beat: dread—the past has found him.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Hiding in a waystation, Wendell studies the map: routes through Thornfell ending at a door beneath the mountain, marked with his family sigil and one word—Sera. Company scouts arrive asking questions; Wendell lies for the first time in years. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Hears Ash
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Introduced in the border town of Cinderhold, Sera is a smuggler-priestess who tends an illegal ember-shrine and hears fragments of a voice no one else can. She recognizes the map's seal when Wendell tries to sell it. Emotional beat: hope flickering against cynicism.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Shrine
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Sera refuses payment and instead offers passage through her hidden roads if Wendell helps her reach the source of the whispers. He agrees reluctantly, telling himself it's about the map, not the name. Vaelric's outriders burn Cinderhold behind them. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged in smoke.

chapters.title: Old Roads, New Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The pair travel smugglers' tunnels where Sera teaches Wendell to listen again; he almost hears something and panics. They find evidence others have died seeking the same door. Emotional beat: fragile trust built in darkness.

chapters.title: The Company's Claim
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. His old captain, Maren, intercepts them—Vaelric has bought the company's loyalty, and Maren offers Wendell amnesty if he surrenders the map. Wendell sees she genuinely believes serving Vaelric protects the free cities. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by love.

chapters.title: Ashes of the House
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Detouring to his ruined childhood home, Wendell finds his father's ledger: payments to the under-court, dates matching his sister Liora's disappearance, and his father's confession that he sold two souls—one was meant to be Wendell's. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as betrayal.

chapters.title: Whispers in the Deep Pass
chapters.summary: POV Sera. In the high pass, Ember's voice comes through Sera clearly for the first time: it names Wendell and begs him to hurry. Pursuers close in; Maren's second-in-command leads the hunt now, not Maren herself. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Split Rock
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A brutal fight in the narrows; Sera is wounded shielding Wendell, and he kills men he trained beside. They escape into a glacial cave where they shelter with refugees fleeing Vaelric's advance. Emotional beat: guilt hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Refugee's Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Sera. An old refugee describes the under-court: souls kept as lanterns, a god caged as its light is drained. Sera realizes Ember isn't silent—it's imprisoned, and her 'whispers' are leaks from the cage. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Maren catches up alone, off the leash, and demands the truth. Wendell shows her the ledger. Torn between her oath to the company and the evidence of Vaelric's soul-trade, she lets them pass—but warns she cannot hold the hunt forever. Emotional beat: bittersweet parting.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Following the map's final leg, they find the door beneath the mountain, sealed with Ishikawa blood. It opens only for Wendell—a lock designed by his father, who built the cage's outer gate. Emotional beat: horror and purpose entwined.

chapters.title: Lantern Court
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Descending into the under-court, they walk halls lit by captive souls. Sera feels each one like a scream. Courtiers—half-faded things—escort them toward the throne, mistaking Wendell for the heir come to claim his inheritance. Emotional beat: vertiginous wrongness.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Vaelric, elegant and reasonable, reveals the truth: Ember's silence was his doing, and the stolen souls power wards protecting the free cities from something worse beyond the mountains. He offers Wendell his sister's freedom in exchange for taking up his father's post as warden. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Liora
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Allowed one meeting, Wendell finds Liora—not a lantern but a prisoner, lucid, who has spent years mapping the cage from inside. She tells him the wards are a lie; Vaelric feeds the souls to himself. Emotional beat: reunion sharpened into conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Warden's Key
chapters.summary: POV Sera. While Wendell plays the dutiful heir, Sera infiltrates the lantern-vault using rites from her shrine days. She discovers the mechanism binding Ember—and that opening it will release everything at once, including the thing Vaelric half-truthfully feared. Emotional beat: courage at the edge of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Vault
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Maren arrives leading Vaelric's guard—amnesty was a trap. But seeing the vault, Maren turns her blade on her own company instead. In the chaos Wendell reaches the cage as Vaelric unmasks fully, no longer pretending to be human. Emotional beat: loyalty repaid at last, war begun.

chapters.title: Ember Unbound
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. To open the cage, someone must anchor the escaping light or the mountain bursts. Wendell offers his name and memories as the anchor—his identity as payment, mirroring his father's sin but reversed into gift. Ember floods free; Vaelric burns. Emotional beat: climax, self-annihilation as salvation.

chapters.title: What Remains of Wendell
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The mountain stabilizes; freed souls rise like embers toward the surface. Wendell stands empty-eyed among them, not knowing Sera or himself. Liora takes his hand and speaks their childhood to him, rebuilding what she can. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness after victory.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Stand
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Above ground, Ember's return ignites every cold altar across the land; the free cities rally, and Maren's company defects wholesale to stand at Thornfell's pass against Vaelric's orphaned armies. Sera becomes the new voice of the hearth-faith. Emotional beat: hope mobilized.

chapters.title: A Name Given Back
chapters.summary: POV Wendell (fragmentary). Months later, Wendell remembers only pieces—but Ember, grateful, begins returning his memories one flame at a time. At a rebuilt shrine, he chooses which self to be going forward, with Sera and Liora beside him. Emotional beat: resolution—identity as something chosen, not inherited.
